newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Court rejects rebidding of Manila Hotel.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects rebidding of Manila Hotel.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Tuesday rejected a government plea for a rebidding of the historic Manila Hotel.

"The Court resolved to deny with finality the motions for reconsideration, as the basic issues raised therein have been passed by the Court and no substantial arguments were presented to warrant the reversal of the questioned decision," the Supreme Court said.

Government lawyers had appealed to the tribunal to allow a rebidding of the hotel after the Supreme Court in a decision on February 3 stopped the state from selling the hotel to Malaysia's Renong Berhad.
Renong had won the bidding for the state-owned property in 1995 but a losing bidder Manila Prince Hotel Corporation went to court.

The Court citing a "Filipino First" policy upheld Manila Prince's contention that the 75-year old Manila Hotel was part of the country's heritage and should not be sold to a foreign group. It ordered the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), which owns the hotel, to sell it to Manila Prince.

Government lawyers had responded by saying the Supreme Court could not force it into selling the property to a local firm. They told the Court the order violated GSIS's rights as hotel owners by depriving them of the chance to get the best possible deal.
On Tuesday, the government said it still disagreed with the Court but that it would abide by the decision.

"The executive department will vow to the decision of the Supreme Court... (But) we still believe that it's wrong," presidential legal advisor Rene Cayetano told reporters after the Court announced its decision.
The Supreme Court's earlier decision had provoked President Fidel Ramos to openly criticise the court for jeopardising reforms for the sake of protectionism.
"I regret the Supreme Court has given the outmoded and failed economic theory of protectionism a new lease on life in this country," Ramos had said in a speech last month.
